report_name: APT29 Targets iOS & Android Users in 'Poisoned Source' Campaign

threat_actors.name: APT29
threat_actors.description: A Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) linked threat group that conducted a large-scale intelligence-gathering campaign named 'Poisoned Source' targeting iOS and Android users. The campaign utilized watering hole attacks and a supply chain compromise of the Plerdy web analytics service.
threat_actors.goals: Intelligence gathering against high-value targets in government, defense, and critical industries.

attack_patterns.name: Drive-by Compromise
attack_patterns.description: Used as the core technique in watering hole and reverse-proxy attacks to inject malicious JavaScript into websites visited by targets.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: Exploited via the supply chain attack on Plerdy, abusing the trust between the analytics service and its client websites to deliver malicious code.

attack_patterns.name: Drive-by Compromise
attack_patterns.description: The mobile-specific equivalent of T1189, used to target iOS and Android users visiting compromised or reverse-proxied websites.

attack_patterns.name: Vulnerabilities
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor acquired and weaponized n-day exploits for iOS and Android devices to use in the campaign.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: APT29 compromised the analytics tracker of Plerdy, a Ukrainian web analytics company, to inject malicious code into thousands of websites using the service.

attack_patterns.name: Browser Fingerprint
attack_patterns.description: A malicious JavaScript injected into compromised websites executed a fingerprinting script to collect browser and device configuration details to identify targets of interest.

malware.name: DarkSword
malware.description: An exploit kit used by APT29 to deliver n-day exploit chains to targeted iOS devices.

vulnerabilities.name: n-day vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.description: Recently patched but not yet widely applied vulnerabilities in iOS and Android were exploited by APT29 to compromise mobile devices. Specific CVEs were not mentioned.

campaigns.name: Poisoned Source
campaigns.description: A large-scale intelligence-gathering campaign attributed to APT29 targeting mobile device users in Ukraine and the U.S. The operation used watering hole attacks and a supply chain compromise of Plerdy to deliver n-day exploit chains.

identities.name: SVR
identities.description: The Russian Foreign Intelligence Service, which is linked to the threat group APT29.

identities.name: Plerdy
identities.description: A Ukrainian web analytics company whose analytics tracker was compromised by APT29 in a supply chain attack.

identities.name: Ukrainian gas producer
identities.description: A legitimate website of a Ukrainian gas producer was compromised in a watering hole attack by APT29.

identities.name: U.S. chemical-industry trade association
identities.description: A legitimate website of a major U.S. chemical-industry trade association was compromised in a watering hole attack by APT29.

identities.name: Bulgarian military-related organization
identities.description: A legitimate website of a Bulgarian military-related organization was compromised in a watering hole attack by APT29.

identities.name: america250.org
identities.description: The official site for the 250th anniversary of American independence, which was cloned using a reverse proxy by APT29 to inject malicious scripts.

infrastructure.name: Watering Hole Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Legitimate, high-traffic websites compromised by APT29 to inject malicious JavaScript for the 'Poisoned Source' campaign.

infrastructure.name: Reverse-Proxy Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: APT29 set up reverse proxies of high-profile websites to inject their malicious script without compromising the original site.

indicators.name: Plerdy Analytics Script Access
indicators.pattern:
title: Plerdy Analytics Script Access
id: 2b8c1a9f-5d7e-4b0c-8a3d-9f1e2d3c4b5a
status: experimental
description: Monitors for access to the Plerdy analytics script (init.js). While often legitimate, a compromise of this script was used in the 'Poisoned Source' supply chain attack. Correlate with other suspicious activity.
references:
  - https://www.sekoia.com/blog/poisoned-source-apt29-watering-holes-targets-mobile-devices-with-n-day-exploits
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-04
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
level: informational
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|contains: '/plerdy.com/init.js'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects web traffic related to the Plerdy analytics script 'init.js'. A compromise of this script was a key part of the 'Poisoned Source' supply chain attack.
